messages.content: Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.
Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.

samples.text: Floating‑point numbers have a limited mantissa, so each arithmetic operation rounds the exact real result to the nearest representable value. When you compute \((a+b)+c\) the sum \(a+b\) is rounded first, and then that rounded value is added to \(c\) and rounded again; computing \(a+(b+c)\) rounds \(b+c\) first, which can produce a different intermediate value and thus a different final rounding. Because the rounding errors depend on the order of operations, the two results can differ, so floating‑point addition is not associative.
